theme: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
queries_run: gh search repos "nyc tlc taxi data" --sort stars
gh search repos "sncf open data OR trenitalia open data OR db opendata" --sort stars (0 results)
gh search repos "flixbus api OR eurostar data OR amtrak gtfs OR amtrak api" --sort stars (0 results, OR syntax likely not effective)
gh search repos "chicago taxi trips" --sort stars
WebSearch site:github.com SNCF open data GTFS/TER (blocked, session WebSearch budget exhausted)
WebSearch site:github.com Deutsche Bahn open data API client (blocked, session WebSearch budget exhausted)

candidates.name: Monthly-Amtrak-Ridership-Forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed monthly Amtrak system-wide ridership series, Jan 1991 - May 2013 (the classic Hyndman/forecasting-textbook Amtrak series), used for R time-series forecasting (ARIMA/exp smoothing). ~269 monthly obs.
candidates.why_useful: Long back-history (22+ years) of a national ground-travel demand series; useful only as a macro travel-demand backdrop / seasonality reference for gap #10 (rail/road capacity), not point-in-time and stops in 2013 so not current.

candidates.name: AMTRAK-Ridership-Forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: Same classic 1991-2013 monthly Amtrak ridership dataset as jimmy-nguyen-data-science's repo, re-hosted for a separate forecasting exercise.
candidates.why_useful: Duplicate of the above; only worth a one-line note since identical series appears in multiple student repos (confirms it's a stable, easy-to-find historical series).

candidates.name: fixed-effects-panel-ols-covid-impact-on-amtrak-ridership
candidates.what_it_holds: Fixed-effects panel-OLS study of COVID's impact on Amtrak ridership; repo built/updated as recently as June 2026, MIT licensed, likely includes a route/state-level panel spanning pre- and post-COVID years (needs a contents check to confirm exact vintage and whether data is route-level or system-level).
candidates.why_useful: If the panel is route- or state-level and covers 2019-2025+, it would be the freshest/most granular Amtrak series found and could proxy regional US ground-travel recovery relevant to domestic leisure travel demand (gap #10); worth a directory-listing check before relying on it.

candidates.name: Amtrak_Ridership_Crawl
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium crawler that scrapes Amtrak's own site for annual ridership by individual station (station-level annual counts, not a national monthly aggregate).
candidates.why_useful: A working method to get station-level Amtrak ridership (finer grain than the national monthly series above); could be adapted to pull current-year station data for a ground-travel cross-check, though it is a scraper of Amtrak.com and would need to be re-run rather than used as-is (no committed data, last updated 2020).
candidates.time_coverage: annual, vintage unclear (crawl-time dependent), repo from 2020
candidates.size_hint: scraper only, no committed data file

candidates.name: amtrak-gtfs-rt
candidates.what_it_holds: A GTFS-Realtime feed generator/parser for Amtrak (live train positions/schedule adherence), actively updated (Apr 2026). No historical ridership counts -- this is train-position/frequency data, not passenger counts.
candidates.why_useful: Could be used to build a service-frequency/capacity proxy for Amtrak corridors going forward (gap #10 capacity angle), but has no historical archive and does not measure ridership or dollars -- weak fit for the ABNB nights/ADR forecast.

candidates.name: UberMovementData
candidates.what_it_holds: Automation script (bachelor's-thesis project) that scraped daily cross-sectional Uber Movement travel-time datasets and merged them into time series, plus EDA/model scripts; outputs CSV. No cities/years specified in README; the tool targets 'any city available on the Uber Movement website' at scrape time.
candidates.why_useful: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Uber shut down the Uber Movement public service in mid-2023, so this scraper now targets a dead endpoint and cannot be re-run; only pre-2023 archived pulls (if the author kept any, unconfirmed) would still exist. Ground-mobility travel-time indices were never a strong ABNB proxy candidate anyway; flag as a documented dead end.
candidates.size_hint: scraper + cleaner scripts, data volume unconfirmed

candidates.name: Uber-movement-bangalore-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed Uber Movement travel-time dataset for Bangalore (city-level speed/travel-time by zone pair), pre-2023 vintage (service discontinued since).
candidates.why_useful: Real committed data, but wrong geography for the ABNB panel (Bangalore is not one of the 13-city or 123-market Inside Airbnb panels) and travel-time data doesn't map cleanly to lodging demand; low relevance.
candidates.size_hint: unconfirmed, likely one or more CSV/JSON exports

candidates.name: chicago-taxi-trips-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis pipeline (AWS EMR/Spark/Zeppelin/Superset) built on the City of Chicago's official Taxi Trips open dataset (data.cityofchicago.org), which itself covers taxi AND transportation-network-provider (rideshare) trips by community area from 2013 to present. Repo itself holds no committed rows; it is a pointer/method against the city's public API.
candidates.why_useful: Chicago is one of the 13 Inside Airbnb panel cities; the underlying City of Chicago Taxi/TNP Trips dataset (linked from this and dozens of similar repos) is a genuinely useful free, granular, long-running ground-transport volume series for that market, even though this specific repo is boilerplate ETL with no unique value beyond confirming the source and query pattern.
candidates.size_hint: external dataset is hundreds of millions of rows; repo has no committed data

candidates.name: nyc-taxi-pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: ELT pipeline (PySpark/dbt/Airflow/DuckDB/Metabase) built against the official NYC TLC Trip Record data (data.cityofnewyork.us / TLC), which includes airport pickup/dropoff flags (JFK/LGA/EWR) by taxi zone, 2009-present monthly Parquet files. Repo itself is boilerplate with no committed rows.
candidates.why_useful: Representative of dozens of near-identical NYC TLC ETL-pipeline repos found in this search; none add unique data, but they collectively confirm the TLC Trip Record Parquet archive (with an airport-trip flag) is the standing free, monthly, decade-plus, one-command-pullable source for gap #10's NYC airport-taxi-trips ask -- worth pulling directly from the TLC site rather than via any of these repos.
candidates.geography: New York City (incl. JFK/LGA/EWR airport trips)
candidates.time_coverage: external dataset 2009-present monthly; repo itself dated 2026
candidates.size_hint: external dataset multi-GB Parquet per month; repo has no committed data

candidates.name: railhead-demo
candidates.what_it_holds: White-label rail-booking demo app that ingests real Amtrak GTFS static schedule data (routes/stops/timetables) with simulated fares/tickets layered on top.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Amtrak publishes a static GTFS feed (schedules/frequency, not ridership or fares) usable for a service-frequency proxy; the booking/fare layer in this repo is entirely simulated so it adds no real pricing data.
candidates.size_hint: GTFS static feed size (~tens of MB), no ridership data

notes: gh search repos hard limit (6 calls) used on: amtrak ridership, nyc tlc taxi data, uber movement, an OR-query for SNCF/Trenitalia/DB (0 results -- gh's search API does not reliably support OR inside a bare query string, so this theme's European rail sources are effectively unsearched), an OR-query for flixbus/eurostar/amtrak-gtfs/amtrak-api (0 results, same OR-syntax problem), amtrak gtfs, and chicago taxi trips. WebSearch was blocked immediately (session-wide budget of 200 already exhausted by other scouts/agents before this task ran), so no site:github.com fallback could be run for SNCF, DB, Trenitalia, Eurostar, or FlixBus -- these remain essentially uncovered by this scout and are a good re-run target once a fresh WebSearch budget or additional gh search calls (split into single-term queries, not OR) is available. Dead end: Uber Movement was discontinued by Uber in mid-2023, so every 'uber movement' repo is now either a stale pre-2023 data dump or a scraper against a dead endpoint -- flag this clearly so nobody re-proposes a live Uber Movement pull. Chicago and NYC taxi/TNP results were dominated (>40 of ~50 hits) by generic student ETL-pipeline boilerplate (Airflow/dbt/Snowflake/Databricks projects) with zero committed data of their own, all built against the same two official city open-data portals (Chicago Taxi/TNP Trips, NYC TLC Trip Record) -- excluded almost all of them per the boilerplate rule, but noted one representative repo for each portal since the underlying portals themselves (not any GitHub repo) are the real gap-10 asset (Chicago = one of our 13 Inside Airbnb cities; NYC TLC = has an explicit airport-trip flag). No FlixBus, Eurostar, SNCF, DB, or Trenitalia repos were found in the searches that did run; a follow-up scout should try single-term gh searches ('flixbus', 'sncf gtfs', 'deutsche bahn api', 'trenitalia', 'eurostar api') and/or WebFetch directly on https://github.com/search?q=... once rate limits clear.
